newsitem.title: FRANCE: French media cautious on EU jobs and growth pact.
newsitem.headline: French media cautious on EU jobs and growth pact.

text.p: Leftist French newspapers offered cautious praise on Tuesday for a European Union pledge to pay more attention to jobs and growth in the run-up to monetary union.

However, right-wing and business dailies were more critical, saying the Amsterdam summit agreement was largely symbolic and would not immediately create jobs in France, plagued by record 12.8 percent unemployment.

EU leaders, responding to French concerns, on Monday issued a resolution putting economic growth and employment at the top of their political agenda. At the same time, they stuck to a "stability pact" to maintain budgetary discipline after the launch of their planned single currency.
The Socialist-led government of Prime Minister Lionel Jospin, which swept to power on June 1, proclaimed it had begun to turn the tide of EU policy.
But the left-centre daily Liberation portrayed the achievement as incomplete.
"A window was opened. Very good," the newspaper said in an editorial. "(But) we are still far from the European growth pact envisioned by the Socialist Party congress."
The French financial daily Les Echos called the last-minute compromise a "face-saving" gesture that allowed all parties to pull back from the brink of rejecting the stability pact.

France had won an expression of EU concern on jobs, the paper said, but had lost out on its other main demands -- to establish a "true economic government" to serve as a counterweight to the planned European central bank, and to launch new major infrastructure projects to reduce unemployment.
"It is true that no country was against Paris' idea that Europe should be concerned about unemployment. But who would be against that?" it asked.
It said a European jobs summit in October would test whether the British, Germans and French could jointly commmit to anything more than vague objectives. "To tell the truth, there is little chance."
The right-wing daily Le Figaro said France, and Europe, had "scored a point".

"Certainly, you cannot make good policy with good wishes, and apparently in this case there is nothing else there. But the European Union had to one day proclaim its concern for its 18 million unemployed. That is what it did yesterday with its social resolution," it said.
The Figaro editorial said Jospin's reliance on the state and the EU to "restart the job creation machine" was misplaced.
"With these solutions, we do not see why he would succeed better than the previous government," it said.
The Communist daily l'Humanite portrayed the jobs and growth resolution put forward by the Jospin government as marking a new stage in the battle against joblessness.

"In fact, a ghost is haunting Europe -- the ghost of unemployment. For the first time it has also haunted the highest circles of diplomacy, disturbing the well-oiled European clockwork...(and) inspiring the drafting of this new text. A new social and political realm is opening in the battle for jobs."
